reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns across instances with external explainability tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both human-intuitive pattern recognition and model-level attribution evidence, increasing the reliability of identifying shared spurious features.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 9686) and assess whether any of them appear non-essential or semantically unrelated to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of common features across all instances and their semantic relevance to income classification

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might a feature that is common in these instances (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse or occupation=Craft-repair) be spurious despite being present in all cases?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis about spurious correlation or bias due to shared, non-informative feature patterns

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance rankings grounded in game-theoretic fairness, helping detect if any shared feature has high attribution despite being semantically irrelevant. LIME offers local interpretability to validate if the model over-relies on specific features in these instances. Integrated Gradients offer gradient-based attribution that reveals smooth influence patterns, useful for spotting spurious feature gradients. Sensitivity analysis directly measures how much prediction changes when a feature is removed, confirming if shared features drive misclassification when they should not.
